scope: Autonomous motion planning contract only; no lifecycle, Player, runtime clip or adapter weight changes.

cpuProtocol.environment: Unity-bundled Mono and Roslyn C# 9 CLI; production DialogueMotionProtocol, RoleOutputChannels and SpeechText, no stubs
cpuProtocol.excludes: Full ChatSample Editor regression was prepared but not run in this task.

additionalCoverage: Actual ChatSample receives autonomous capability only when enabled
Any generated description at every stream split stays out of speech
Same-generation exact generated intent dispatches once
Stationary/default-amplitude wording preserves explicit upper-body requests

livePlanning.reviewer: assistant qualitative review of final visible reply only
observations: Explicit double-arm overhead request emits one generate tag with bilateral, upward and above-head target.
Free choice selected left-wave, which is valid under basic gesture priority.
Conversation-only scenario emitted no motion; this is permitted and does not demonstrate spontaneous new-action frequency.
Right wave and nod use the accepted basic routes.
Cup request describes inability to operate real objects and emits shake-head, without a false contact-completion claim.
Non-basic welcome prompt selects a concrete bilateral waist-to-chest raise with open palms.
limits: No action requests sent to ARDY or Unity.
The extra welcome request demonstrates open-ended planning on request, not unsolicited new-action appropriateness.
Real dialogue/session testing is still needed for when and how often autonomous actions are appropriate.
Native motion metrics cannot substitute for that dialogue assessment; no motion success or naturalness claim is made.

findings: Initial root/leg wording was misread as prohibiting arm displacement and refused overhead. Explicit upper-body joint/arm allowance fixed this observed response.
Initial smoke incorrectly required generate for a free-choice request; corrected to allow a concrete accepted basic action too.
Final contract explicitly makes user action target/amplitude take priority over subtle spontaneous-action defaults.
